core_obligations: Form the scheme theoretic image Z of the diagonal morphism V -> Y x_S U and note that an admissible blowup of Y replaces Z by its strict transform (proof lines 9772-9776).
Apply the Zariski-after-blowup input to assume, after passing to a further V-admissible blowup, that Z -> Y is an open immersion (proof lines 9776-9777).
Let V' be the image of Z in Y and conclude that V' -> U is proper, because Y x_S U -> U is proper and V' is isomorphic to the closed subscheme Z of that fibre product (proof lines 9778-9781).
proof_roadmap: Take the scheme theoretic image of the diagonal and track it through blowups (proof lines 9772-9776).
Use the Zariski-after-blowup input to make it an open immersion (proof lines 9776-9777).
Read off properness of the induced morphism from the closed immersion into the proper fibre product (proof lines 9778-9781).
difficulty_reason: For a quasi-compact quasi-separated base S, a scheme U of finite type and separated over S, a quasi-compact open V of U with a compactification V inside Y over S, the lemma produces a V-admissible blowup Y' -> Y and an open V inside V' inside Y' such that V -> U extends to a proper morphism V' -> U (statement lines 9761-9769). The proof forms the scheme theoretic image Z of the diagonal morphism V -> Y x_S U, and uses two inputs in sequence: that replacing Y by a V-admissible blowup replaces Z by the corresponding strict transform, which is exactly the strict transform comparison lemma proven just before, and then the Zariski-after-blowup lemma, which allows one to assume Z -> Y is an open immersion (proof lines 9772-9777). If V' denotes the image of Z in Y, then V' -> U is proper because the projection Y x_S U -> U is proper and V' is isomorphic to the closed subscheme Z of that fibre product (proof lines 9778-9781). Chaining the strict transform comparison with the Zariski-after-blowup input to make the image an open immersion is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
